title: Update icons, support icon aliases, add icon type preference arg
description:
This updates the icon set to `FontAwesome 6.2.0`, which contains 2,016 free icons across the regular, solid, and brand types. This also includes an alias lookup table to make it possible to reference icons by previous names. For example the old icon names `"contact-card"` and `"vcard"` map to the canonical name of `"address-card"`. A warning is issued, stating the current in-use name, but the icon will be provided.

Another change adds the preference for the icon type. Typically, for the free icons, an icon either has:

(1) solely a brand type or a solid type
(2) both a regular type and a solid type

For the second case, there is now a `prefer_type` argument (default: `"regular"`) that allows for a choice when specifying the icon using a short name.

Fixes: https://github.com/rstudio/fontawesome/issues/94
Fixes: https://github.com/rstudio/fontawesome/issues/69
Fixes: https://github.com/rstudio/fontawesome/issues/95

title: Check if used in knitr only. Warn and ignore in that case.
description:
This closes #82 

Choice here is to do like unsupported format : Warn and Ignore when we detect no `knitr::pandoc_to()` formats, meaning **rmarkdown** is not used, only `knitr::knit()` directly. 

Usually, we don't know for sure the output format in that case where YAML header is not used. 

However, we could try support it if you want (for Rnw to .tex for example, or Rmd to .md). We would test `knitr::out_format()` in that case, but I am not sure how reliable this is, and it is possible that the output document after does not support our assumption. 

That is why I am thinking limiting to **rmarkdown** only seems easier and enough. 

I upgrade suggest requirement to 1.31 for `knitr::pandoc_to()` but we could keep the old way if you prefer.

title: Bugfix and enhancement to left/right margins in `fa()`
description: This PR makes `margin_right` argument functional in the `fa()` function, defaulting to the `"auto"` margin (essentially `0`, same as before the update). I believe the default (besides being hardcoded) provides too much space to the right of icons and isn't ideal when putting several icons in a row (screenshot of rendered .Rmd included below). With this, I'd like to add a `margin_left` argument (also with an internal default of `"auto"`) Fixes: #53 .Rmd document ```` --- title: "fontawesome_test" output: html_document --- ```{r setup, include=FALSE} knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE) ``` ```{r load_packages, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE} library(fontawesome) ``` # Just a few tests with `r fa("font-awesome-logo-full", fill = "forestgreen")` It works well in headings... # `r fa("r-project", fill = "steelblue")` H1 Heading ## `r fa("r-project", fill = "steelblue")` H2 Heading ### `r fa("r-project", fill = "steelblue")` H3 Heading #### `r fa("r-project", fill = "steelblue")` H4 Heading ##### `r fa("r-project", fill = "steelblue")` H5 Heading ...and works equally well within inline text: `r fa("r-project", fill = "steelblue")`. Here are some inline icons `r fa("r-project")` `r fa("ad")` `r fa("apple-alt")` `r fa("bullhorn")` `r fa("compass")` within text. Icons have `auto` (usually computed as `0`) margins on both sides. Proposed default. Here are some inline icons `r fa("r-project", margin_right = "0.2em")` `r fa("ad", margin_right = "0.2em")` `r fa("apple-alt", margin_right = "0.2em")` `r fa("bullhorn", margin_right = "0.2em")` `r fa("compass", margin_right = "0.2em")` within text. Icons have `0.2em` right margins. This is the hardcoded default. Here are some inline icons `r fa("r-project", margin_left = "0.2em", margin_right = "0.2em")` `r fa("ad", margin_left = "0.2em", margin_right = "0.2em")` `r fa("apple-alt", margin_left = "0.2em", margin_right = "0.2em")` `r fa("bullhorn", margin_left = "0.2em", margin_right = "0.2em")` `r fa("compass", margin_left = "0.2em", margin_right = "0.2em")` within text. Icons have left and right margins of `0.2em` (possible with the proposed `margin_left` and functional `margin_right` args). ````

title: Specify version explicitly in update script
description:
This changes the update script so that it downloads files from a specific tag. This makes the result of the update script repeatable, and not dependent on the current state of an external data source.

Also, the master branch of the FortAwesome/Font-Awesome repo does not always correspond to a release; this change ensures that if the version is reported to be 5.15.3, we are actually downloading files from that release.

title: knit_print support for non HTML format
description:
This will close #42 

Here is a first draft on how it could work. Basically you convert the svg to image and include that in the resulting document. 

# About HTML output

`fa()` will inherit the `html` class so we let next method (the one in **htmltools** handles the `knit_print()`. 

If we don't want to rely on other package method we could do it directly, same as `htmltools::knit_print.html()`

* Transform as character
* Write as-is in the output, with maybe protection like `htmltools::htmlPreserve` (or just inline raw format attribute `{=html}` directly. 

# About the syntax used to include in non HTML format

At first I was using `\includegraphics` in TeX directly, but we can let Pandoc to the conversion for inline image and generate the markdown code. 
We can also revert easily to inserting LaTeX directly, protected as raw inline or not if you think it is better to not let Pandoc handles it.  See https://github.com/rstudio/fontawesome/pull/43/files/999a4a95d2805c59e9b73aef6eebec74d5b41da3
Using markdown gives us support for docx output. 

## About docx support 

For docx output, I used png file because using svg was not working as expected as it should (https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/topic/insert-icons-in-microsoft-office-e2459f17-3996-4795-996e-b9a13486fa79). I believe there could be an issue with pandoc conversion. Svg file is inserted but can't be read in the docx document, whereas if I drag and drop the file it works.

## What is left 

- [ ] size of the icon: should we retrieve infos inside the svg ?
- [ ] multiple svg passed to `fa()`: how to knit_print ?

### About the size.

Currently it uses a default of `1em` for eight at the insertion. Writing to file use default size - width is not specified at insertion, but we could.

I believe retrieving the size requires to use **xml2** to parse the svg code ?
Unless they are passed as attributes in the `fa()` object. 

## About multiple icons

Passing multiple icons in `fa()` will result in one character string 
``` r
res <- fontawesome::fa(fontawesome::fa_metadata()$icon_names[1:3])
str(res)
#>  'fontawesome' chr "<svg aria-hidden=\"true\" role=\"img\" viewBox=\"0 0 448 512\" style=\"height:1em;width:0.88em;vertical-align:-"| __truncated__
```

From `knit_print()` point of view, this is ok for HTML because it will use the svg code asis. But for non HTML format we need to generate images. With the logic fro above, it would be one file per icon, so we would need to know how many icons - either by parsing the string to several svg, or `fa()` should not return a string bu a list of icon, and methods `as.character.fontawesome` or `format.awesome` would concatenate all the svg icons to one long string.
If we have a list, `knit_print` could create a file for each icon and include them all.

I am creating this as draft PR for now because we need to discuss above topics to finalize something to really review and merge. Hope it is ok.

title: Add accessibility features to generated icons via `fa()`
description:
This adds new arguments to `fa()` (`a11y_case` and `title`) to help generate SVG tag attributes for accessibility (`title`, `aria-hidden`, and `role`). The accessibility cases match the use cases for the SVG icons ('decorative' and 'semantic'). The default is 'decorative', meaning that SVG icons generated by `fa()` are accessible by default. The 'semantic' case uses the `aria-labelledby` attribute, combined with a `<title>` tag just before the SVG `<path>` sibling tag.

Fixes: #38

title: SVG compatibility with IE11
description: This PR includes an icon sizing scheme and the addition of width and height attrs so that inline SVGs will render correctly in IE11.

title: Update internal data so that V4 names can be used with `fa()`
description:
This PR consolidates the data processing scripts into one and adds the `v4_name` column to the internal `fa_tbl` table that's used to look up the SVG code from the icon name. This provides an opportunity to locate the appropriate SVG icon from a version 4 name. This uses the YAML file that defines the translation from v4 to v5.

We also store the current version of FA release in an internal vector. This allows us to report on which version of the icons the package has.

Fixes: https://github.com/rstudio/fontawesome/issues/31
Fixes: https://github.com/rstudio/fontawesome/issues/30

title: Changes to reduce dependencies, signal for pkg installation (`rsvg`)
description:
These changes address a few issues related to dependency reduction (number of package imports and lowering the min version of R). With this, only htmltools is now required. The need for `rsvg` in `fa_png()` is now checked at the beginning of the function body, providing a useful message if the package is missing. 

Fixes: #32
